events.title: Union of the Crowns: James VI of Scotland Becomes James I of England
events.description: Queen Elizabeth I of England died in the early hours of March 24, 1603, and James VI of Scotland, her cousin's son, was proclaimed her successor as James I of England and Ireland, bringing the thrones of England and Scotland under one monarch.
events.significance: Marked the beginning of the personal union of the Scottish and English crowns, a key step toward the eventual formation of Great Britain and the end of the Tudor dynasty.

events.title: Robert Koch Announces the Discovery of the Tuberculosis Bacterium
events.description: German physician Robert Koch presented his discovery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the bacterium that causes tuberculosis, to the Berlin Physiological Society.
events.significance: The discovery enabled the diagnosis and later treatment of a leading cause of death in the 19th century and earned Koch the 1905 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. World Tuberculosis Day is observed on this date to commemorate it.

events.title: The Great Escape from Stalag Luft III
events.description: On the night of March 24-25, 1944, 76 Allied prisoners of war escaped through a tunnel from the German camp Stalag Luft III. Most were recaptured, and 50 were executed on Hitler's orders.
events.significance: The escape became one of the most famous prisoner-of-war breakouts of World War II and was later dramatized in the 1963 film The Great Escape. The executions were prosecuted as war crimes after the war.

events.title: Assassination of Archbishop Óscar Romero
events.description: Salvadoran Archbishop Óscar Romero was shot dead while celebrating Mass in San Salvador, a day after he had called on soldiers to stop obeying orders to repress and kill civilians.
events.significance: His killing intensified the tensions that led to the Salvadoran Civil War. Romero became a symbol of resistance to oppression and was canonized by Pope Francis in 2018.

events.title: Exxon Valdez Oil Spill
events.description: The tanker Exxon Valdez ran aground on Bligh Reef in Prince William Sound, Alaska, spilling roughly 11 million gallons of crude oil.
events.significance: One of the largest oil spills in U.S. history, it devastated wildlife and local fishing communities and led to the Oil Pollution Act of 1990, strengthening spill prevention and response regulation.
